docs.title: Microphone Detection Subsystem
docs.text:
Team 203 | Fall 2026

External Design Review — October 26, 2026

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
This individual engineering datasheet documents my design and development work for EGR 304 — Embedded Systems Design at Arizona State University.

My assigned subsystem focuses on detecting and conditioning an audio signal from a microphone so that it can be processed by a PIC18F57Q43 microcontroller.

This website serves as a living engineering document containing the design decisions, component selections, electrical schematics, power calculations, and supporting documentation for the subsystem.

docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text:
The microphone detection subsystem is designed to receive an acoustic signal, condition the signal using analog circuitry, and provide a suitable electrical signal to the microcontroller for processing.

The proposed design includes:

  • A microphone for converting sound into an electrical signal.
  • An MCP6004 operational amplifier for analog signal conditioning.
  • Resistors and capacitors for signal filtering and biasing.
  • A PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano development board for signal processing.
  • An LM7805 voltage regulator providing a regulated 5 V supply.
  • An external 9–12 V DC power source.

The design is currently in the preliminary development stage. Final component specifications and operating limits will be confirmed through datasheet verification and testing.

docs.title: My Individual Contribution
docs.text:
My responsibilities for the microphone detection subsystem include:

  • Developing and documenting the subsystem block diagram.
  • Researching and evaluating electrical components.
  • Preparing the bill of materials (BOM).
  • Designing the electrical schematic.
  • Developing the preliminary subsystem power budget.
  • Evaluating component compatibility, power requirements, and design constraints.
  • Maintaining engineering documentation for design reviews.

docs.title: System Operation
docs.text:
The intended signal path is:

Acoustic Input → Microphone → Analog Signal Conditioning → PIC18F57Q43 Microcontroller

The microphone produces an electrical signal corresponding to the incoming sound. The analog conditioning circuit amplifies and filters the signal before it reaches the microcontroller.

The microcontroller can then sample the conditioned signal using its analog-to-digital converter (ADC).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This block diagram illustrates the major components and signal connections for the Team 203 microphone detection subsystem.

The microphone converts acoustic signals into electrical signals. These signals are amplified by a Microchip MCP6004 operational amplifier and passed through a low-pass filter before reaching the ADC input on the Microchip PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano development board.

The microcontroller converts the amplified microphone signal into a digital value using its 12-bit ADC. The signal can then be reproduced through the 8-bit DAC or transmitted to other team subsystems using UART communication.

The PCB pushbutton provides a digital input to the microcontroller, while the red LED receives a digital output from the microcontroller.

The power architecture uses an external 9–12 V DC power supply and an LM7805 linear voltage regulator to provide a regulated 5 V rail.

docs.title: Component Selection — Microphone Subsystem
docs.text:
EGR 304 | Team 203 | Joseph White

Updated: November 25, 2026

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The microphone subsystem detects sound for the team's interactive cat-toy project. An analog electret condenser microphone feeds a signal-conditioning amplifier and low-pass filter, which supplies the RA0 ADC input on the PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano.

The subsystem uses an external 9 V DC wall adapter and an STMicroelectronics L7805ABV voltage regulator to provide a regulated 5 V supply.

Components were evaluated based on electrical compatibility, power consumption, PCB integration, cost, availability, and audio performance.

docs.title: 1. Microphone Selection
docs.text:
The following microphones were evaluated during the preliminary design phase.

Solution Pros Cons 3S 3SM121MZB1UAAnalog MEMS microphoneDigiKey 66 dBA SNRLow power consumptionSingle-ended analog output Requires 1.6–3.6 V supplySmall LGA packageRequires additional voltage regulation 3S 3SM122KZB1VD-002-RAnalog MEMS microphoneDigiKey Small footprintLow power consumptionSingle-ended output Requires lower-voltage supplyDifficult to hand solder Syntiant SPH11C3LR5H-1Differential analog MEMS microphoneDigiKey High SNRGood noise rejectionWide audio frequency response Differential output increases circuit complexityRequires lower-voltage supply Option 4 — Existing two-wire electret condenser microphone Already availableSimple analog interfaceEasy to assembleNo separate 3.3 V regulator required in the implemented circuit Manufacturer and exact part number unidentifiedElectrical specifications are not fully documented

docs.title: Selected Microphone
docs.text:
Choice: Option 4 — Two-wire electret condenser microphone.

The original MEMS microphone options required additional voltage regulation and more complicated PCB assembly.

The existing electret condenser microphone was selected because it was already available and could be integrated into the analog signal-conditioning circuit using a simple resistive bias network.

Characteristic Selected Component Microphone type Electret condenser Output Analog Connections Two-wire Manufacturer Unidentified Part number Unidentified Bias supply 5 V rail through 2.2 kΩ resistor Schematic reference MK1 Availability Owned

The microphone is biased through resistor R6. Capacitor C4 provides AC coupling between the microphone and amplifier circuit.

The selected microphone was installed on the manufactured subsystem and tested during hardware verification.

docs.title: 2. Operational Amplifier / Signal Conditioning
docs.text: Solution Pros Cons Microchip MCP6004-I/PQuad operational amplifier, DIP-14DigiKey Operates from 1.8–6 VCompatible with 5 V supplyRail-to-rail input and outputLow current consumption Four amplifier channels may be unnecessary1 MHz gain-bandwidth product Microchip MCP6002-I/PDual operational amplifier, DIP-8DigiKey Smaller packageLow power consumptionRail-to-rail operation Only two amplifier channelsRequires schematic and footprint changes Texas Instruments LM324ANQuad operational amplifier, DIP-14 InexpensiveFour amplifier channelsSingle-supply operation Not rail-to-railReduced output swing near positive supply rail

docs.title: Selected Operational Amplifier
docs.text:
Choice: Microchip MCP6004-I/P.

The MCP6004 was selected because it operates from the regulated 5 V supply and provides rail-to-rail input and output capability.

The amplifier increases the microphone signal amplitude before the signal is passed through the low-pass filter and sampled by the microcontroller ADC.

Characteristic Specification Manufacturer Microchip Technology Part number MCP6004-I/P Package DIP-14 Supply voltage 5 V in this subsystem Amplifier channels 4 Gain-bandwidth product 1 MHz Schematic reference U3

Manufacturer Datasheet

docs.title: Amplifier and Filter Configuration
docs.text:
The microphone amplifier uses an inverting configuration with a 1 kΩ input resistor and a 100 kΩ feedback resistor.

The nominal inverting-stage voltage gain is:

\[ A_v=-\frac{R_8}{R_5} =-\frac{100000}{100} \times\frac{100}{1000} =-100 \]

A 10 kΩ potentiometer provides an adjustable reference voltage for the non-inverting input.

The low-pass filter consists of resistor R9 and capacitor C5.

Component Value R9 220 Ω C5 0.22 µF

The nominal low-pass filter cutoff frequency is:

\[ f_c=\frac{1}{2\pi RC} \] \[ f_c=\frac{1}{2\pi(220)(0.22\times10^{-6})} \approx3288\text{ Hz} \]

docs.title: 3. Power Regulation
docs.text:
The microphone subsystem requires a regulated 5 V supply.

Three voltage regulator options were evaluated.

Solution Pros Cons Option 1 — STMicroelectronics L7805ABV5 V linear regulatorTO-220 package Already availableSimple circuit designLow output noiseThrough-hole assemblyUp to 1.5 A with appropriate operating conditions Linear regulator produces heatRequires adequate input voltage and thermal management Traco Power TSR 1-24505 V switching regulatorDigiKey High efficiencyLower heat dissipationWide input voltage range Higher cost1 A maximum outputPossible switching noise Option 3 — Texas Instruments LM7805CT/NOPB5 V linear regulatorTO-220 package Simple circuit designThrough-hole packageSimilar functionality to selected regulator Produces heat during operationRequires thermal managementWould require purchasing another component

docs.title: Selected Voltage Regulator
docs.text:
Choice: STMicroelectronics L7805ABV.

The L7805ABV was selected because it was already available, provides a regulated 5 V output, and can be integrated into the PCB using a simple through-hole footprint.

Characteristic Specification Manufacturer STMicroelectronics Part number L7805ABV Regulator type Linear Output voltage 5 V Rated output current Up to 1.5 A, subject to thermal limitations Package TO-220 Subsystem input voltage 9 V DC nominal Schematic reference U1 Availability Owned

STMicroelectronics L78 Series Datasheet

docs.title: Thermal Considerations
docs.text:
Linear regulator power dissipation is approximately:

\[ P=(V_{IN}-V_{OUT})I_{OUT} \]

At an example subsystem current of 100 mA:

\[ P=(9-5)(0.1)=0.4\text{ W} \]

Actual regulator power dissipation depends on the measured subsystem current.

docs.title: 3.3 V Regulation
docs.text:
A separate 3.3 V regulator was considered during preliminary design because the original MEMS microphone candidates required a lower supply voltage.

The final implemented design uses an electret condenser microphone with a resistive bias circuit. Therefore, a separate 3.3 V regulator is not included in the manufactured subsystem.

docs.title: 4. External Power Supply
docs.text:
Three external power supply approaches were considered.

Solution Pros Cons Option 1 — Model 0930, 9 V DC / 3 A wall adapter Already availableCompatible with barrel jackProvides sufficient input voltage for L7805ABVContinuous power during testing Requires AC wall outletNot portable Option 2 — 12 V DC wall adapter Commonly availableProvides adequate regulator input voltage Increases linear regulator heat dissipationRequires AC wall outlet Option 3 — 9 V battery supply PortableNo wall outlet required Limited operating timeReduced current capabilityRequires battery replacement or charging

docs.title: Selected External Power Supply
docs.text:
Choice: Model 0930 AC/DC wall adapter.

The selected adapter was already available and provides the nominal 9 V DC input required by the microphone subsystem.

Characteristic Specification Manufacturer Unbranded Model 0930 Type AC/DC wall adapter AC input 100–240 VAC Input frequency 50/60 Hz DC output 9 V Rated output current 3 A Rated output power 27 W Barrel connector polarity Center positive Availability Owned

The external power supply connects to barrel jack J1. A 1 A fuse provides input protection before power reaches the L7805ABV voltage regulator.

docs.title: Power Architecture
docs.text:
9 V DC Wall Adapter → J1 → 1 A Fuse → L7805ABV → Regulated 5 V Supply

The regulated 5 V supply powers the microphone bias circuit, operational amplifier, microcontroller, and indicator LEDs.

docs.title: 5. Microcontroller Selection
docs.text:
Selected Microcontroller: Microchip PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano

The PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano is the development board used for the microphone subsystem.

Characteristic Specification Manufacturer Microchip Technology Microcontroller PIC18F57Q43 Development board Curiosity Nano Configured clock frequency 64 MHz ADC resolution 12-bit DAC resolution 8-bit Communication UART Programming interface USB onboard debugger Schematic reference U2

Microchip PIC18F57Q43 Product Information

docs.title: 7. Team Connector Configuration
docs.text:
The microphone subsystem includes an eight-pin connector for interfacing with other team subsystems.

Connector Pin Signal Signal Type 1 DAC_OUT Analog 2 RA0_ADC Analog 3 UART_TX Digital 4 UART_RX Digital 5 INT_OUT Digital 6 BTN Digital 7 LED Digital 8 GND Common ground

These assignments represent the designated connector signals. Final physical connections and team communication compatibility must be confirmed during team integration.

docs.title: 8. Hardware Verification
docs.text:
The custom microphone subsystem PCB was manufactured, assembled, programmed, and tested.

The microcontroller verification firmware performs the following functions:

  • Reads the amplified microphone signal using RA0.
  • Converts the 12-bit ADC reading to an 8-bit DAC value.
  • Reproduces the analog signal using the DAC.
  • Transmits microphone readings using UART1.
  • Provides ADC and DAC readings through PuTTY.
  • Controls the PCB red LED using the PCB pushbutton.
  • Controls the Nano LED using the Nano pushbutton.

Individual subsystem hardware verification was demonstrated to the instructor.

Final team communication and integration remain separate development activities.

Microcontroller Code

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
The final microphone subsystem uses an electret condenser microphone, Microchip MCP6004-I/P operational amplifier, STMicroelectronics L7805ABV voltage regulator, and Microchip PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano.

The subsystem is powered by a model 0930 external 9 V DC wall adapter.

The final component selection eliminates the need for a separate 3.3 V voltage regulator and simplifies PCB assembly.

The manufactured subsystem has completed individual hardware verification. The remaining project activities involve final team communication and system integration.

docs.title: Power Budget — Microphone Subsystem
docs.text: EGR 304 | Team 203

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The microphone subsystem uses a 9–12 V DC input and an LM7805 linear voltage regulator to provide a regulated 5 V power rail. This rail supplies the PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano development board and the microphone signal-conditioning circuit.

The following power budget is preliminary. Current values are design estimates pending verification against the final component datasheets.

docs.title: Section A — Component Current Requirements
docs.text:
Component Supply Voltage Estimated Current PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano 5 V input 100 mA MCP6004 operational amplifier 5 V 5 mA Microphone circuit 5 V 1 mA Total 106 mA

The values above are preliminary allowances, not confirmed absolute maximum currents. Additional small loads, including the indicator LED, must be checked before finalizing the budget.

docs.title: Section B — Power Rail and Safety Margin
docs.text:
The subsystem uses one regulated 5 V rail.

Parameter Value Estimated component current 106 mA Required safety margin 25% Safety margin current 26.5 mA Estimated current requirement 132.5 mA Estimated 5 V load power 0.6625 W

The 25% safety margin is applied to the estimated operating current:

106 mA × 1.25 = 132.5 mA

docs.title: Section C — Voltage Regulator
docs.text:
The selected regulator is the LM7805 linear voltage regulator.

  • Input: 9–12 V DC
  • Regulated output: 5 V DC
  • Regulator output current requirement: approximately 133 mA, based on preliminary estimates

At the maximum 12 V input, estimated regulator power dissipation is:

P = (12 V - 5 V) × 0.1325 A

P = 0.9275 W

This is a preliminary conservative calculation using the margin-adjusted current. Thermal performance must be checked before final PCB fabrication.

docs.title: Section D — External Power Source
docs.text:
The subsystem is designed to use an external 9–12 V DC supply through a barrel jack.

The final power supply must support the subsystem's maximum current requirements with the specified safety margin. A specific adapter's rated output current must be confirmed before calculating remaining available current.

docs.title: Section E — Battery Life
docs.text: Battery life is not applicable because the current design uses an external DC power supply rather than a battery.

docs.title: Design Conclusions
docs.text:
The preliminary budget indicates that the microphone subsystem has relatively modest power requirements. A single regulated 5 V rail simplifies the design and reduces the number of required power components.

The primary concern identified is heat dissipation in the LM7805 regulator, particularly when operating from a 12 V input.

Before finalizing the design, the maximum current consumption of each active component, the complete load current, the selected adapter's current rating, and the regulator's thermal performance will be verified.

  • Displays ADC and DAC readings in PuTTY.
  • Controls the PCB red LED using the PCB pushbutton.
  • Controls the onboard Nano LED using the onboard pushbutton.

docs.title: Appendix — Microphone Subsystem
docs.text: EGR 304 | Team 203 | Joseph White

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This appendix provides supporting technical information for the microphone detection subsystem of the automated cat-toy project.

The subsystem uses the microphone supplied during EGR 304 laboratory exercises, an MCP6004 operational amplifier, and a PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano microcontroller.

docs.title: Main Components
docs.text: Component Part Number Purpose Microcontroller PIC18F57Q43 Signal processing and communication Microphone Class-supplied two-wire microphone Acoustic detection Operational amplifier MCP6004 Microphone signal conditioning Potentiometer XCHC Electron 3296W-103 Adjustable voltage reference Voltage regulator LM7805 Regulated 5 V supply Pushbutton Momentary switch User input Indicator LED Red LED Visual status indication

docs.title: Microphone Signal Conditioning
docs.text:
The microphone detects acoustic signals and provides an electrical signal to the MCP6004 operational amplifier.

The amplifier conditions the microphone signal before it reaches the microcontroller's analog-to-digital converter (ADC).

A 10 kΩ multiturn potentiometer provides an adjustable reference voltage for the amplifier.

The potentiometer is adjusted to approximately 2.5 V to establish the desired reference level.

docs.title: Potentiometer Connections
docs.text: Potentiometer Pin Connection Pin 1 +5 V Pin 2 (Wiper) MCP6004 reference input Pin 3 Ground

docs.title: Microcontroller Pin Configuration
docs.text: PIC Pin Function Purpose RA0 ADC input Conditioned microphone signal RA1 GPIO output INT_OUT RA2 DAC output Analog output RC6 UART TX Serial transmission RC7 UART RX Serial reception RD1 GPIO input Pushbutton RD2 GPIO output Red LED

docs.title: Power System
docs.text:
The subsystem uses an external 9–12 V DC supply.

An LM7805 linear voltage regulator provides a regulated 5 V supply for the circuit.

The design uses a single regulated 5 V power rail.

The 10 kΩ potentiometer establishes an adjustable reference voltage of approximately 2.5 V for the amplifier.

No additional 3.3 V regulator is required for the selected design.

docs.title: Signal Flow
docs.text:
1. The class-supplied microphone detects sound.
  2. The MCP6004 amplifies and conditions the microphone signal.
  3. The 10 kΩ potentiometer establishes the amplifier reference voltage.
  4. The conditioned signal enters the PIC18F57Q43 through RA0.
  5. The microcontroller processes the ADC readings.
  6. UART1 provides communication with the other team subsystems.
